correctness.rationale: Odd bases have exact valuation-preserving differences, giving a first-period permutation. Even bases become affine from n=k. For each odd b, the missing target b(k-1) is avoided by a valuation-one base 2u: small k explicit, larger k by power-map fiber counts in units mod 2^s and a strict union bound. The finite checker exhaustively covers k<=8 and corroborates larger cases; no unproved infinite step is inferred from finite data.

value.rationale: An exact optimal worst-case first-covering time for all dyadic moduli and all odd coefficients replaces a published general quadratic bound with a sharp linear-plus-logarithmic law. The existence of extremal even bases requires a nonroutine counting argument. It supplies a complete natural modulus family of a published modular exponential coverage problem rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
